title: Remaining headroom
summary: Headroom: usage left vs. an even pace to the reset. A pool's headroom is one worker's remaining full-rate runway divided by the time to its reset, and every display prints it as N% of even pace, so a reading above 100% means usage is behind an even pace. Level placement splits it among the live workers and unregistered launches on the same machine whose model the pool covers, plus the new launch, and ranks options by that per-worker share. Level launches place one at a time, so a burst spreads across pools instead of piling onto the one that looked emptiest before it started. While a surface's fresh read fails for any reason but a rejected sign-in (such as an idle Claude CLI whose token expired), its relay keeps the last read windows, with their original observation time, until each resets, so placement still ranks that surface.
